devin_acme: Hey — after rotating our API key we started seeing 401 invalid_api_key from the Redwood API when calling from Cloud Run. Quick repro:

devin_acme: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Token "A3fG...xY==\n" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

carol_support: Thanks. Two quick questions: did you update the secret in Secret Manager as a raw string? Any proxy or middleware that might re-encode headers? Also note our API recognizes the schemes "ApiKey" or the header "x-api-key" — "Token" isn't supported.

devin_acme: We used Secret Manager and the CI pulls the secret into an env var. The value in SM looks like: "A3fG...xY==\n" (it includes the quotes and a newline). No other proxy besides Cloud Run. 

sam_support: That explains it — the quotes + trailing newline will make the header invalid. Common pitfalls: secret stored as JSON/quoted string, CLI copy added quotes, or editors inserting CRLF. Also some HTTP clients will silently drop Authorization on redirects, but your curl shows header present. You can repro locally by setting the env variable with a trailing newline:

sam_support: ```bash
export REDWOOD_KEY='"A3fG...xY==\n"'
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models
# -> 401 invalid_api_key
```

sam_support: Fix: store the key as the raw token (no quotes/no newline) or trim in your start script. Example fixed header:

sam_support: ```bash
export REDWOOD_KEY='A3fG...xY=='
curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models
# -> 200 OK
```

deploy-bot: Deployment finished 2 mins ago (cloud-run/service-abc rev-42)

devin_acme: Confirmed — removed quotes/newline in Secret Manager and redeployed. Calls now succeed. Thanks!

carol_support: Great — closing this thread. :tada:
